title: Bounded Temporal-Certificate Cost and Reference Runtime Overhead Characterization

qualified_cost_shape.benchmark_transaction_harness: TX_TEMPORAL_EXTERNAL_FULL_HALF, full plus two-half branch, identical in A and B

qualified_wall_clock_characterization.interpretation: Microsecond-scale incremental cost was observed on the stated GitHub runner. These values characterize this frozen implementation, fixture matrix, compiler and hardware environment; they are not universal time bounds.

negative_evidence_and_correction.falsified_assumption: TX_TEMPORAL_NONE could be used as a valid one-trial acceptance-neutral benchmark route
negative_evidence_and_correction.source_reconciliation: valid_policy admits only TX_TEMPORAL_EXTERNAL_FULL_HALF and TX_TEMPORAL_MODEL_CERTIFICATE
negative_evidence_and_correction.resolution: The failed assumption is retained in the correction artifact; the benchmark was redesigned on the existing valid full/two-half route without weakening physical, mass or solve-equivalence gates.

architecture_invariant_audit.3_explicit_data_separation: PASS: H_budget remains numerical configuration and derivative history remains optional numerical continuation data rather than physical storage.
architecture_invariant_audit.4_compact_persistent_state: PASS_WITHIN_SCOPE: only active temporal-history layouts carry one n-element history vector; inactive layouts carry none.
architecture_invariant_audit.5_scratch_per_worker: PASS_WITHIN_SCOPE: indicator arrays are transient, not committed state; PE06 adds no persistent solver scratch. Reusable worker-scratch optimization remains a future performance option.
architecture_invariant_audit.7_transactional_timesteps: PASS: correctness and timing use existing checkpoint/trial transaction machinery; rejected experimental benchmark assumptions never alter production semantics.
architecture_invariant_audit.9_generic_time: PASS_WITHIN_SCOPE: frozen VQ34 non-calendar horizons are reused; no day-boundary assumption is introduced.
architecture_invariant_audit.13_mass_conservation_absolute: PASS: hard mass gating remains active and A/B physical mass results are bitwise identical in the checked pre-timing matrix.
architecture_invariant_audit.16_multiswap_primary_use: PASS_AS_CHARACTERIZATION_ONLY: O(n) memory and microsecond service cost are quantified; no claim is made that current per-call allocation is already optimal for very large MultiSWAP batches.
architecture_invariant_audit.23_physics_solver_policy_separated: PASS: no physical option or reference-solver tolerance changes between A and B; benchmark temporal tolerance is identical scaffolding in both arms and is not a production policy.
architecture_invariant_audit.24_predictable_compute: PASS_FOR_BOUNDED_CHARACTERIZATION: incremental solve topology is fixed and executable-proven; median/p95/max observations are recorded without converting finite-run evidence into a universal wall-clock guarantee.
architecture_invariant_audit.25_reference_mode_available: PASS: the measured path is the full reference Richards implementation.
architecture_invariant_audit.26_runtime_diagnostics: PASS: existing diagnostics expose principal and incremental solve counts needed for attribution.
architecture_invariant_audit.27_optional_functionality_scales_with_us: PASS_WITHIN_SCOPE: history and indicator work occur only for the active temporal-history layout/service.
architecture_invariant_audit.30_architecture_change_audit: PASS: final pre-closeout diff contains no production source modifications and all applicable invariants are explicitly reconciled.

hard_nonclaims: F-PE06 does not select, recommend or qualify a numeric H_budget.
F-PE06 does not define or qualify BALANCED or THROUGHPUT policy.
F-PE06 does not establish a universal hardware-independent runtime bound.
F-PE06 does not claim that the full/two-half benchmark route is the production model-certificate execution route.
F-PE06 does not authorize any mass-conservation or physical-fidelity concession.
F-PE06 does not qualify parallel real-physics MultiSWAP scaling or worker-count scaling.
F-PE06 does not optimize the current per-call temporal-service allocations.

future_optimization_candidates: remove one or both previous-derivative copies where interface ownership permits
reuse the sixteen indicator work vectors from worker scratch rather than allocate per call
re-run PE06-equivalent characterization after any such optimization against the unchanged reference-mode semantics
